criterion_text.edit-frame-trace: With GITTURTLE_TRACE=1 the editor prints gitturtle.theme_edit_frame_ms=<ms> exactly once per burst of live-preview edits and once per open, and nothing without the variable. The value starts at entry to the token row's change handler (the hex Input's InputEvent::Change or the ColorPicker's change, before the value is parsed) and ends inside the paint closure of a zero-size trace element that the root render defers at a priority above the dialog layer (Root::render_dialog_layer), so it is the last element Window::draw paints in the first frame drawn after the handler applied the draft, whether that draw runs in the frame tick or synchronously in Window::dispatch_key_event. It therefore contains the parse, the readability recompute, apply_appearance and the request_layout, layout, prepaint and paint of the whole window, and excludes next-frame callback waits, frame-finish bookkeeping, present and input delivery. Editor opens and edits no longer print theme_apply_frame_ms, whose switch boundary is unchanged. A #[gpui::test] asserts one line per edit whose end stamp is taken during that frame's paint after the dialog layer and never from a next-frame callback; docs/benchmarks/metrics.md defines the new metric with this boundary and its exclusions and removes the editor sentences from the switch metric's entry.
criterion_text.edit-budget: In release mode at 2x on the themes-apply-trace fixture with History at 1 to 1000 and the 2,000-line Split comparison retained (the state of docs/benchmarks/2026-09-19-theme-editor.md), on a fresh version-6 store seeded with 32 custom themes (the bound: Seed 01 to Seed 32, bases cycling ThemeChoice::ALL, one token differing from the base, theme midnight, follow-system off), with the editor opened by Edit… on the first row (New theme… is disabled at the bound) and 60 valid Canvas hex edits in six dialogs of ten (the procedure of the 2026-09-19 record), each edit at least 1.2 s apart, cycling dark canvases that keep the Readability list empty, in one recorded launch designated in writing before it runs: gitturtle.theme_edit_frame_ms p95 ≤ 26 ms over the 60 pooled edits, the p95 being the 57th of the 60 sorted samples (owner decision of 2026-09-20, re-cut from 24 to 26 ms by owner decision of 2026-09-21 after candidates ea31261, 2030b3d and 23ee777 measured 26.348, 24.440 and 25.191 ms on this boundary with about 3 ms of launch-to-launch spread and the remaining elements reported as the editor dialog's kit Input and ColorPicker internals); the first dialog's ten edits are reported as the designated set and carry no bound. The bound sits at this boundary's draw plus about 2 ms of handler and apply: the diagnosis measured the draw at 19.5 ms on the empty store and 26.4 ms with 32 themes on the unvirtualized candidate, and puts the realistic floor after the row virtualization and layout wins at 15 to 19 ms. docs/benchmarks/ gains a dated record with the build identity (--build-info and executable SHA-256), host, cache state, the seed store's digest, raw samples for the 60 edits with the designated ten identified, the same procedure on an empty store, UI-thread CPU per edit, elements per frame before and after, and the dominant remaining cost; the performance-reviewer attests it with `python3 scripts/agent-loop.py attest --kind performance`.
criterion_text.switch-no-regression: The same record shows 60 Settings theme switches by real pointer clicks cycling ThemeChoice::ALL on the empty store and on the 32-theme store, measured as in docs/benchmarks/2026-09-18-theme-apply.md: UI-thread CPU per switch (main-thread schedstat delta from the release to 150 ms after it) median ≤ 23 ms on the empty store (base 5637cec measured 26.4 ms with the save completion's second render, 58b6226 without it 21.0 ms) and no more than 4 ms higher on the 32-theme store, which shows the rows no longer cost every Settings frame (3 ms until 2026-09-22; widened to 4 ms by the coordinator under the owner's 2026-09-21 instruction that a few ms off is acceptable, after 85a7d07 measured +3.402 with switch-frame element counts identical to 23ee777, whose delta was +1.565, on a pass whose every UI-thread CPU figure ran 2 to 4 ms above the previous one because the IDE renderer held the load near 2.8); and gitturtle.theme_apply_frame_ms, unchanged at its next-frame-callback boundary and blind to draw cost, stays at median ≤ 8 ms and p95 ≤ 16 ms on both stores as a non-regression.

gitturtle.theme_edit_frame_ms.what_the_value_spans: Stamped at entry to ThemeForm::hex_changed (theme_editor.rs:1568-1569, trace_stamp before the parse) inside the 7th key's InputEvent::Change; a valid value reaches draft_changed (line 1632) and preview_theme_draft (line 575), which keeps the first stamp of the burst in State::edit_started (line 586) and calls apply_appearance (line 593). The root render (views.rs:2459-2464) takes the stamp after Root::render_dialog_layer and appends edit_trace_probe (theme_editor.rs:625-659): a zero-size canvas deferred at priority usize::MAX (EDIT_TRACE_PRIORITY, line 322), whose paint closure prints the line (line 637). It is the last element Window::draw paints in the first frame drawn after the draft, whether the platform tick or Window::dispatch_key_event draws it. The value holds the parse, the readability recompute, apply_appearance and the whole window's request_layout, layout, prepaint and paint with the dialog over it; it excludes next-frame callback waits, frame-finish bookkeeping, present, pre-handler input delivery and GPU execution. The frame-tick grid does not enter the value.
gitturtle.theme_edit_frame_ms.lower_bound_by_construction: none from the frame grid: the end stamp is taken inside the draw, not at a tick

gitturtle.theme_apply_frame_ms.what_the_value_spans: Unchanged in kind, 45 lines lower in settings.rs than on 23ee777 (rows_off_boundary was added above choose_theme): stamped at choose_theme entry (settings.rs:547); apply_appearance (line 554), save_preferences (line 555), then trace_next_frame (line 557, main.rs:1353) registers a next-frame callback that prints. Next-frame callbacks run only on the platform frame tick, before that frame is laid out and painted, so the value is the handler plus the wait to the next tick of the 8.334 ms X11 grid and is blind to the draw. It cannot fall below the handler's own cost, and its spread is the keystroke's phase on the grid; UI-thread CPU per switch is the instrument for the frame's cost.
gitturtle.theme_apply_frame_ms.lower_bound_by_construction: handler cost + phase on the 8.334 ms grid (0 to one period)
